turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come sit, ma'am. Pressure is one twenty eight over eighty two, pulse 76. Doctor is ready.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please. You have someone with you?

[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I am her husband, doctor. She is having heel pain since three months. Morning time she is not getting up properly, she just sits on the bed. And she is running daily, that is why.
[SEG0004] person_4 (PATIENT): Arre, I can't hear myself think. It is two months, not three. I do get up. I have a shop to open, I am not sitting there like some patient.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. You tell me then.

[SEG0006] person_4 (PATIENT): Right heel. The first steps in the morning are bad, like I have overdone it. After I walk around a little it eases. By evening I feel like a wet rag, the standing itself finishes me.
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Eight in the morning to nine at night she is standing, and we live just above the shop, so she never really leaves the place.
[SEG0008] person_4 (PATIENT): Till seven thirty, not nine. Yes, we live upstairs, but that is not the heel. Don't stretch the story.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. How much are you running?
[SEG0010] person_4 (PATIENT): Three or four times a week, not daily. Two, three kilometres, that is all. Umm, and when I first put the foot down, my feet feel dead.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): When you say the feet feel dead, do you mean numb, or tingling, or is it the pain only?
[SEG0012] person_4 (PATIENT): No. Not numb. No tingling. Just heavy and painful, and I am tired of explaining it.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any swelling on that heel?
[SEG0014] person_4 (PATIENT): No swelling.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does it wake you at night, or only those first steps?
[SEG0016] person_4 (PATIENT): Only the morning. Night is fine. I just want to sleep, I am so done with this.
[SEG0017] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She bought new shoes last week also, soft ones. Still she is limping the whole morning.

[SEG0018] person_4 (PATIENT): Last month, not last week, from Bata. The pain was already there before the shoes. I limp for a minute only, then I walk, and I have a frog in my throat trying to get a word out while you talk.

[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): So one of you says two months, one says three, I will keep it as roughly two to three months and not fight over the date. Err, first-step heel pain, some running, long hours standing, and the shoes came after the pain started.
[SEG0020] person_4 (PATIENT): So what is it? Say it plain, I am fed up.

[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): The usual picture is plantar fasciitis, and that is my working impression. It could also be heel pad pain from the standing, so I am keeping both. I am not concluding a stress fracture, there is no night pain, and I am not ordering any test or x-ray today.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me press. Inner side of the right heel, yes, this spot is tender. I do not see any swelling, and the calf squeeze is not painful.
[SEG0023] person_4 (PATIENT): Ah, that spot, yes. Don't press so much.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any diabetes, or thyroid, any illness that is ongoing?
[SEG0025] person_4 (PATIENT): No. Nothing of that sort.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Are you taking any medicine? And any reaction to a drug ever, penicillin or anything else?

[SEG0027] person_4 (PATIENT): Crocin 500, one tablet, only when the heel is too much, maybe three times in a week. No, never, I have taken penicilin and everything, it was fine, even last year for the throat.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good, so no known drug allergy. I am not starting any tablet. What I want is calf stretches, and a heel insole.
[SEG0029] person_4 (PATIENT): Stretches. The shop is open at eight, when am I doing all that?

[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Before you step down in the morning, stretch the calf, hold for thirty seconds, three times, both legs. In the evening roll the foot on a bottle. Kindly do it every day, that is what helps this.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): For the shoes, get a soft heel insole, a cushion under the heel, and use it in the shop footwear as well as for running. Any chemist will keep it.
[SEG0032] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will see to it that she does the stretching.
[SEG0033] person_4 (PATIENT): I will do it myself. He fusses too much, and I am already irritable.
[SEG0034] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry, doctor, the next one is asking for you. Ma'am, there is no old file here, the folder is empty.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): That is fine. No scan from my side. Also bring the running down to twice a week until this settles, but keep walking in the shop, don't rest it completely.
[SEG0036] person_4 (PATIENT): Twice a week, hmm. And if it just stays like this?
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back if it is not better in four weeks. If it is easing, no need to hurry back. We can review it then.

spec.situation: Runner or shop worker with heel pain on the first steps in the morning for two months; new shoes mentioned; doctor suggests stretches and insoles; no tests.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

bad.reason: All details supported except transcript says both legs, not each side.
bad.text: Calf stretches for 30 seconds, three times each side, before stepping down in the morning, and roll the foot on a bottle in the evening, daily (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=patient)

omissions.text: Patient described the heel/feet on first putting the foot down as feeling 'heavy and painful' / 'feet feel dead' rather than numb or tingling.

No known drug allergy was specifically clarified to include penicillin/other drugs; patient said she had taken penicillin before without reaction.
Doctor documented that he was not starting any tablet.
Doctor stated he was not ordering any test or x-ray today / no scan from his side.
Doctor noted he was not concluding a stress fracture because there was no night pain.
